headline: A storefront and its backend, built to be checked.
ledeMetrics: VERSIONED REST /api/v1 · ZOD-VALIDATED · README + CURL + POSTMAN
problem: A company take-home assessment: demonstrate genuine full-stack capability inside a fixed window. The real user is a reviewer with limited time — every feature has to be findable, runnable, and checkable without a walkthrough call.
constraint: About two weeks, solo, from an empty repository. The scope had to be real enough to prove data modeling and validation depth without ballooning past what a reviewer can reasonably evaluate.
decision: Treat the reviewer as the user. Backend: a versioned REST API (/api/v1) so changes can't silently break consumers, nested product/variant data modeling in Prisma over PostgreSQL, and defensive Zod validation returning proper 400s with readable messages instead of crashes. Frontend: React + TypeScript + Vite + DaisyUI covering the storefront's honest complexity — category filtering, product detail with size-variant selection, a cart with live count, out-of-stock states, and a full checkout flow. Documentation as a first-class deliverable: README with setup and endpoint reference, curl examples, and a Postman collection.

evidence.caption: The out-of-stock grid states and variant selection are where the data model earns its keep — the UI renders what the schema already knows.

result.label: DELIVERED
result.metrics: API v1 · ZOD-VALIDATED · README + CURL + POSTMAN · ~2 WEEKS
result.body: Complete storefront and hand-built Express/Prisma/PostgreSQL backend, finished in about two weeks. This record deliberately closes on technical scope — it exists to prove the full-stack half of the title, and every claim is reproducible from the repository.
